transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I’m just tired all the time and don’t have the energy to do much of anything anymore, even the stuff I used to enjoy. My wife eventually insisted I get checked out because it's been going on for quite a while now.
How long have you been feeling this way continuously, and have there been any periods of at least two months when you felt back to your usual self?

This low, worn-out feeling really settled in about two or three years ago, not long after I started phasing into retirement. It has pretty much stuck with me ever since, without any real breaks or times where I felt back to my usual self.
Besides the low energy and loss of interest, have you also been feeling down or hopeless most days, or is it mainly the tiredness and lack of enjoyment?

It’s really both, to be honest. On top of the tiredness, I have this low, gray cloud hanging over me most days, and I often catch myself thinking "what’s the point?" even when I’m out fishing or sitting with my grandkids.
Have these symptoms become so severe that they’ve made it very hard for you to function day to day, such as taking care of yourself, doing household tasks, or leaving the house?

Yes, they've definitely impacted my daily life over the past couple of years. I've backed out of community activities, missed several appointments, and my wife has had to pick up the slack around the house because I struggle to keep up with things I used to handle easily.

Over these past couple of years, have you had other symptoms like changes in sleep or appetite, trouble concentrating, feeling guilty or worthless, moving or speaking more slowly, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

My sleep and appetite are definitely off—I lie awake with my mind spinning about wasting retirement, wake up too early, and often forget to eat during the day only to mindlessly snack at night. I haven't noticed moving or speaking slowly, and while I don't have thoughts of self-harm, I do often find myself wondering "what's the point?" when doing activities.
Before these past 2–3 years, did you ever have a period of at least 2 months when your mood and energy were back to normal, or have you felt somewhat down most of your adult life?

Before I started phasing into retirement about three years ago, my mood and energy were completely normal and I felt like myself. This low, worn-out feeling only settled in and became a constant presence after I transitioned out of my full-time work.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a sustained depressive syndrome for 2–3 years with persistent low mood, marked loss of interest/pleasure, low energy, sleep and appetite disturbance, impaired concentration/rumination, and clear functional impairment. Symptoms have been continuous without remission for at least two months and there is no history suggestive of mania, psychosis, or a chronic lifelong depressive pattern. The presentation is most consistent with a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms.
